quarters.summary: Reliance Industries Ltd anticipates continued growth across its segments, with a focus on expanding its digital services, retail, and new energy initiatives, despite challenges in the oil and gas sector due to geopolitical tensions.

Rupee depreciation was a concern, with an 11% decline for the year and 4% in March.

subsections.label: Forward crude cover / inventory position

subsections.label: Refining: strong cracks + high utilization; Bina standout
points: Core driver: cracks unusually strong, specifically diesel (HSD) and ATF cracks very high.
Utilization: combined ~84%, with Bina ~87% and Kochi ~85% noted as better performers.
Bina advantage attributed to crude slate flexibility: it can process majority high sulfur crude, which was comparatively cheaper than low sulfur.

subsections.label: Marketing: adverse margins, inventory effect, pricing response, network strength
points: Elevated international product prices late in the quarter led to adverse marketing margins.
BPCL responded with calibrated retail price revision of approximately ₹7.5/litre across MS and HSD.
BPCL disclosed a positive marketing inventory impact of ~₹3,000 crore as advanced gain/loss.
Domestic sales volume: 13.62 MMT.
Retail continuity: petrol/diesel supplies largely uninterrupted.

Non-retail/commercial: diesel volumes dipped due to shift from direct to retail, reduced volumes where BPCL would not sell below standard margin, and some product unavailability as refinery streams were diverted to LPG.

subsections.label: Capex execution & project updates (Project “Aspect”)
points: Geopolitics impacted supply chain/procurement/execution, but no significant impact on the critical line items; long-lead equipment already ordered.
Mumbai Refinery PRFCC: 7% complete, commissioning targeted Sept 2029.
Kochi polypropylene: 40% complete, commissioning targeted May 2028.
POL and LOBS installations progressing in line with the plan.
New refinery project: land registration for ~3,082 accounts completed; environmental clearance expected by Q2 FY26-27 with final approval expected shortly.

points: BPCL acquired remaining 39.14% in IBV Brazil (from Videocon Energy Brazil), making it a wholly-owned subsidiary of BPRL.
Accounting impact: exceptional income from FCTR reclassification—management stressed purely accounting… no incremental cash flow.
Project development: operator signed FPSO contract; expected timelines: First oil FY30-31, first gas FY31-32.
Project expected ~88,000 bpd, with BPCL group effectively holding 40% project interest.

subsections.label: Cost headwinds
points: Management explicitly tied landed-cost inflation to freight + insurance + supplier premium, with spot tightness forcing premia.

subsections.label: LPG and gas: supply assurance, demand controls, compensation buffer
points: LPG: supply constraints + anti-diversion controls + structural PNG shift.
BPCL maintained LPG supply via diversified imports and maximized refinery LPG output; also implemented measures under the government’s direction to manage demand-supply.

Domestic LPG volumes fell ~14–15% (double-digit degrowth) in Q1, driven by some supply shortage, tighter delivery/booking controls: >90% digital bookings and delivery confirmation via SMS, PNG substitution: ~30,000–40,000 connections surrendered from LPG as PNG expanded in connected areas.

Under-recovery per cylinder (management provided CP-based snapshots): July CP under-recovery ~₹490/cylinder; With August CP $592, under-recovery about ₹210 (with caveat it may change if CP rises again).
LPG compensation: large and growing receivable buffer.
As of June 30, 2026, cumulative LPG compensation buffer: ₹15,804 crore, after adjusting for installments received against the announced compensation of ₹10,594 crore.
Management stance: continued engagement with GoI; remain confident of their continued support though timing is the issue.
Gas business continuity amid LNG disruption.
Despite force majeure under two major LNG long-term contracts, BPCL supplied bulk CNG/PNG customers uninterrupted by spot LNG procurement.
Sales growth: Bulk gas sales +3% YoY, GA (city gas) volumes +60% to 85 TMT.

key_takeaways: Integrated model matters: management pushed back on viewing marketing losses in isolation when cracks are extreme—“not fair… to see marketing under recovery” without refining uplift.
Cost headwinds are multi-factor (not just freight): management explicitly tied landed-cost inflation to freight + insurance + supplier premium, with spot tightness forcing premia.

LPG remains a large earnings swing factor via the ₹15,804 crore compensation buffer and ongoing under-recovery volatility; BPCL is tightening controls and leaning on PNG substitution in connected areas.
Project execution continuing despite geopolitics: capex guidance unchanged; large commitments already placed; management claims critical path protected.
Upstream optionality strengthening with Mozambique progress and Brazil consolidation/FPSO contracting—cash flow still several years out, but milestones advanced during the quarter.

points: Refining margin contraction offset by marketing tailwinds; management credited retail fuels and easing LPG losses.

subsections.label: Q1 FY26 Operational Performance (Refining, Marketing, Gas)
points: Refining: High utilization at 118% of nameplate; lower GRM due to inventory build-up.
Product cracks: gasoline $9.88/bbl, gasoil $15.81/bbl.
Russian crude sourcing expected to remain in the 30–35% range as long as no new sanctions are imposed.
Higher crude inventories driven by geopolitical concerns, with normal crude inventory at 2.3–2.4 MMT, but held 2.9–3.0 MMT.
Marketing: Strong retail fuel contribution; direct diesel competitive pressure noted.
Network additions in Q1: 317 new ROs; 99 new CNG stations. Total network: 23,958 ROs; 2,607 CNG stations.
Throughput leadership: 153 KL/month per RO, outperforming PSU average.
LPG losses have decreased, and management is not participating in the direct diesel discount game.

subsections.label: Capex, Major Projects, and Execution Updates

Kochi Polypropylene project progress at 12.2% vs schedule 16%; spend ₹260 crore, commitment ₹1,200 crore.
Mumbai Refinery upgrade approved with gross capex of ₹14,200 crore, targeting mechanical completion by May 2029.
Greenfield refinery/petrochemical complex in Andhra Pradesh with board-approved ₹6,100 crore for pre-project activities.
Renewable/green energy projects include 100 MW wind contracts and JV NeuEn Green Energy with Sembcorp.

Russian discount compression has prompted agile sourcing of alternatives to maintain economics.

subsections.label: Marketing profitability drivers

key_takeaways: IMF upgraded 2025 global growth to 3%; India FY’25 outlook 6.4%; RBI retained FY’26 GDP growth at 6.5%.
Refining: High utilization at 118% of nameplate; lower GRM due to inventory build-up.
Marketing: Strong retail fuel contribution; direct diesel competitive pressure noted.
Capex guidance for FY26 is ₹20,000 crore, with peak capex expected in FY28 and FY29.
Management flagged uncertainty from Aug’25 US tariff measures, but cited resilient domestic demand.
BPCL is not participating in the direct diesel discount game, leading to temporary share softness.
Mumbai Refinery upgrade approved with gross capex of ₹14,200 crore, targeting mechanical completion by May 2029.
